MRP1 is the major transporter for the efflux of GSH, cysteinyl leukotrines and their metabolites from cells.
MRP1 is not a drug resistance transporter but rather a transporter of importance in the etiology and/or progression of a wide variety of human diseases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MRP1 plays a key role in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis and cancer, and that MRP1 may serve as a target for the development of new therapies for these diseases.

MRP1 plays a key role in regulating the intracellular levels of lipid-derived mediators, and thereby influences the etiology, progression, and outcome of a host of diseases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MRP1 is an integral part of the body’s defense against oxidative stress, and that it may play a role in the regulation of inflammation and the immune system.
